basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: The built artifact itself with its fabric and geometry, not the facility that operates it.
Decomposes into storeys, elements and installed systems, while rooms as occupied spaces belong to the space model.
Separate from the land parcel and site on which it stands.
Records measured condition and hazards of the structure, not the works project that built or repairs it.

may: Record measured properties and condition observations with method and date.
Read geometry and element data to plan safe movement or inspection.
Report defects and hazards to the responsible party.
Project the record to exchange formats with a declared loss inventory.
mustNot: Certify structural safety or fitness for occupation.
Alter structural, fire-protection or egress elements by remote control or instruction.
Enter restricted or unsafe zones flagged in the record.
Overwrite earlier condition assessments instead of adding new ones.
Publish detailed plans of security-sensitive buildings.
requiresHuman: Structural or fire safety assessments and sign-off.
Decisions on demolition, closure or evacuation.

considerations: Wrong structural or fire data can cost lives in an emergency.
Accessibility information decides whether disabled people can enter and leave safely.
Detailed building data can enable burglary or attacks if disclosed.
Embodied carbon and energy performance affect the environment for decades.

items: Gross and net floor area in square metres, measured to a stated standard.
Height in metres above a stated datum, to roof or highest point as declared.
Footprint geometry in a declared coordinate reference system.
Thermal transmittance of envelope elements in W/(m2 K), measured or calculated per method.
Indoor air temperature in degrees Celsius and relative humidity in percent, with time and location.
Structural deflection or crack width in millimetres, with gauge position and date.
A building is recognised by footprint, height, facade features, entrances and an address or identifier plate.
It is confused with adjoining buildings sharing walls, with temporary structures and with the facility or site it belongs to.
Fire spread and blocked escape routes.
Asbestos, lead paint and other hazardous materials in old fabric.
Falls from roofs, openings and stairs.
Brick Schema for installed building systems.
